title: Planner: AI-generated status reports in Planner Agent
summary: The rollout, licensing and control instructions are supported. The auditing question is too broad: Microsoft documents auditing for Copilot user interactions, including the Copilot conversation in which these reports are generated; uncertainty should be limited to report-specific events.

claims.quote: To turn on Planner Agent and Planner Agent chat for a specific security group: ... Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowPlannerCopilot $true -PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId <security group id>

claims.claim: Planner policy changes can take up to one hour to take effect.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly confirmed that the Planner PowerShell setting governs this new Copilot-app report capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Agent AI generated status reports disable separately admin UI AllowPlannerCopilot security group settings; "PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId" "admin center". Read turn-off-planner-agent and MC1506735; neither ties this setting to the new Copilot-app reports.

claims.claim: The Planner PowerShell article directs administrators to the Microsoft 365 admin center guidance for Planner Agent in Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: Disabling Loop affects other Planner and Loop experiences, so it is not a report-only control.
claims.quote: When Loop is disabled, users cannot create Loop task lists, so no tasks sync into Planner from them. Tasks users create directly in Planner are not affected.
